description: pyspaceweather is a Python wrapper for the Australian Bureau of Meteorology's Space Weather API, which provides near real-time data from the Australian Space Weather Forecasting Centre. Each API request method, for example the current magnetic alert for the Australian region, geomagnetic indices and warnings, is exposed as a method that returns typed Python objects with start and end times, G-scale values and descriptions. It was written by an independent developer, Ben Nour, and published on PyPI as version 0.1.0 in June 2024, with documentation on Read the Docs and automated tests. Coverage is the Australian region served by the Bureau. Format and access: a pip-installable package; users need a free API key from the Bureau's registration page. Licence: MIT; free. Caveats: a single early release by one maintainer, so API changes on the Bureau side may break it. It supports automated data preparation for hazard exposure and emergency response studies of geomagnetic storms on Australian grids and pipelines. A related catalogue record is the Bureau's World Data Centre for Space Weather, which holds the longer archives.
